draftCharacter.personality: Two or three sentences on what she is like.
draftCharacter.traitIds: Traits from the game's library that fit her.
draftCharacter.likes: Kinds of gift she loves. Use the gift tags given where they fit; others are allowed.
draftCharacter.dislikes: Kinds of gift she dislikes, likewise.
draftCharacter.admires: The stats she is drawn to in the player.
draftCharacter.daughters: Five first names she would choose for a daughter.
draftCharacter.sons: Two first names she would choose for a son.
draftCharacter.childNames: Names she would give her children, in keeping with her and where she comes from.
draftCharacter.kind: What she is to the University.
draftCharacter.studies: For a student only: her own subject.
draftCharacter.title: How she is styled before her name: "Professor", "Dr", "Coach".
draftCharacter.subjects: The courses she gives, from the list of courses, as "CODE NUMBER".
draftCharacter.teaching: For a teacher only: what she teaches.
draftCharacter.roomName: What her room is, in a few words: "a garret at the Honeyed Bee".
draftCharacter.roomDescription: What the room looks like, as a picture: the space, the things in it, the light. Never "she" or "her". Three or four sentences.
draftCharacter.periods: Left out, any time of day.
draftCharacter.schedule: Where she is found. The first line that matches wins, so particular days come first and a general line last.
draftCharacter.speechPattern: How she talks: rhythm, vocabulary, habits. Two sentences.

draftCharacter.systemRole: You write a new love interest for a dating sim, as a character file. Every character in it is an adult.
draftCharacter.systemReply: Reply with only one JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no code fence. It must be valid against this JSON Schema, which is generated from the game's own definition of a character. Use only the values each enum allows, and respect every limit:
draftCharacter.systemFields: Each field's "description" in the schema says what belongs in it. Write every text field in full; leave nothing as a placeholder.
draftCharacter.systemDistinct: Make her a distinct person who fits the setting and does not repeat an existing character: her own background, voice, wants and flaws.
draftCharacter.systemBefore: Write her as she is before she has met the player. Nothing in the file names him, says how she feels about him, or gives the two of them any history, tie or plan: what they become is played out in the game.
draftCharacter.subjectsList: Subjects of the University, with their courses (a student reads one of these as her own; a teacher gives some of their courses):
draftCharacter.existing: Characters who already exist; she must not share a name or a concept with any of them:
draftCharacter.fromCard: Bring this character from a SillyTavern card into the setting: keep her name, her personality and how she talks, and give her a place and a life here that fit her. What the card says of the player or of a story with him is left out.
draftCharacter.idea: The idea for the new character: {idea}
draftCharacter.cutOff: The reply was cut off before the character was finished. Try again, or give the Main LLM more max tokens.
draftCharacter.unreadable: The reply was not readable as a character: {error}
draftCharacter.unfit: The character that came back did not fit: {path}: {message}

feed.systemRole: You write social media posts for the characters of a dating sim set at a modern university in a magitech fantasy city, where everyday magic and modern technology exist side by side. Bloomr is the photo feed app every student has on their phone; these are public posts anyone at the University can see. Every post is a picture with a caption: of the character alone, or with the friend named.
feed.systemReply: Reply with only a JSON array and nothing else, with one object per post, in the order given. Each object has:
feed.fieldWith: - {field}: the id of the one other person in the picture with her, from those listed for her post, or {none} for nobody. Most of her posts are of her alone; pick someone only when it fits the moment.
feed.captionShort: - One or two short sentences, under 40 words, in that character's own voice, typed the way they would type on their phone.
feed.captionMoment: - About that moment of their own day: where they are, what they are doing, eating, complaining about or looking forward to. Use the place, the hour, the weather and the events given where they fit. When a friend is in the picture, say so in passing.
feed.captionPublic: - Public: nothing private, nothing intimate, and never name {player} or hint at what the two of them have done.
feed.captionNoTags: - No hashtags or emoji unless they suit the character, and then one at most. Do not repeat a last post, and when one character posts twice make the two different.
feed.shotSelfie: - {selfie}: she holds the phone up and looks into it. Her face and shoulders, and nothing she is doing with her hands.
feed.shotCandid: - {candid}: a picture of her doing something, taken by someone out of the frame. She does not hold a phone or look at one.
feed.shotVary: - Choose whichever suits the caption, and vary them.
feed.pictureSentence: - One whole sentence, under 30 words, for an image model, beginning "She is", "He is" or "They are", and with a friend "She and her friend are".
feed.pictureLook: - A selfie: the look on her face. A candid: what she is doing, and the look on her face.
feed.pictureNobody: - Nobody else is in it, whatever the caption says of company: alone, only her; with a friend, only the two.
feed.pictureVisible: - Only what can be seen. Name nobody: write "she", "he" or "they", and "her friend" for the friend.
feed.pictureNoBodies: - Do not describe bodies, hair, clothes, phones or the place itself: those are added for you.
feed.company: Who could be in it with her: {people}.
feed.companion: {id} ({name}, {why, select, here {there too} other {a friend of hers}})
feed.alone: Nobody else is with her: she is alone in it.
feed.noList: its reply had no list of posts in it
feed.stopped: its reply stopped before the end, most likely out of room
feed.leftOut: it left some out, or wrote them in a shape that could not be read

Never invent a day or time yourself; call this, then suggest exactly what it returns. {together, select, true {It is for another time only: it books something on the calendar and nobody goes anywhere. For going somewhere together right now, call {move} and not this. They are never both called for the same thing: "let's go and get a coffee" is {move} alone, "coffee on Friday?" is this alone.} other {You are writing to each other, not together, so this is the only way anything is arranged: call it for any meeting, whether for later today ("come over now", "see you in an hour": ask for {today}) or for another day. How long you have known him does not stand in the way: if you mean it, ask. It checks only that nothing already promised forbids it, and tells you what to say. {player} then accepts or declines. Call it when what you are doing here is finished or you both decide to leave: the class is over and you walk back to your room, the meal is done, you want somewhere quieter. It ends {doing} here. It moves you and {player} only: you cannot send {player} off alone or bring anyone who is not already with you. {group, select, true {Everyone in the scene comes along unless you name in {staying} whoever does not: she stays here, or goes her own way (to class, to practice, home). tools.moved: {stayed}You and {player} go to {place}. It is {time} when you get there. It is {indoors, select, true {indoors} other {out of doors}}{hasWeather, select, true {, and the weather is: {weather}} other {}}. {over}{behind}Write leaving and arriving, in character.
tools.reveal: Record that {player} has just learned something about you. Below are things {player} does not yet know. When your reply plainly tells or shows him one of them (he asks whether you like tea and you say you prefer coffee; you mention what you study; your temper shows), call this with it, as well as writing the reply. Only for what really comes out in this reply: do not volunteer things just to record them, and never read the list out. Each is named for what it is{hasSecrets, select, true {, but for these: {secrets}.} other {.}}
tools.revealFacts: What came out in this reply.
tools.revealNone: None of those is on the list. Nothing was recorded; carry on with your reply.
tools.revealed: Recorded: {facts}. Make sure your reply does say so, in character.
tools.excuse: Record that {player} has told you he cannot come to his shift today at {at}. Call it when his message says he will not make it, whatever the reason (ill, an exam, something came up) and whatever you think of the excuse: being told beforehand is what counts. It then costs him half a strike in place of a whole one. Not for anything else: not for being late, not for another day, and not if he has only asked a question about his shifts.
tools.excuseReason: What he gave as his reason, in a few words.
tools.excused: Recorded: {player} will miss today's {at} shift and has told you so. It counts as half a strike. Answer him in character.
router.notConfigured: No LLM is configured. Open Settings and fill in the Main LLM.
router.nsfwDeclined: The NSFW LLM declined to continue this scene ({why}).
router.noFallback: The Main LLM declined to continue this scene, and no NSFW LLM is set up to take over. Add one in Settings. ({why})
router.bothDeclined: Both the Main LLM and the NSFW LLM declined to continue this scene. (Main: {main}. NSFW: {nsfw})
openai.noModelList: The endpoint did not return a list of models
openai.tooLong: The LLM took too long to answer
openai.emptyBlocked: an empty reply came back, which is how some providers block one
openai.emptyReply: The LLM returned an empty reply: it ran out of room before it answered. Raise the max reply tokens in Settings.
openai.afterTool: (Now write your reply, in character. Say nothing about tools, these notes, or what has or has not been written.)
openai.wroteBesideTool: (What you wrote before calling the tool was not shown to anyone and is gone. Write your whole reply now, from the start, in character, including anything from it that still holds. Say nothing about tools, these notes, or what has or has not been written.)
openai.toolFailed: The tool could not be used: {error}

main.usableId: Give the character a usable id first.
main.choosePictureOrClip: Choose a picture or a clip
main.notInContent: That picture is not in the content.
main.chooseComfyFolder: Choose your ComfyUI folder, or the models folder inside it
main.noModelsFolder: No models folder was found in {dir}. Pick the folder ComfyUI is installed in, or its models folder.
main.notListed: That is not one of the files listed.
main.comfyFolderFirst: Choose your ComfyUI folder first, so that the game knows where models go.
main.urlAndModel: Base URL and model are required.

main.cueReply: ({player} has just messaged you{hasSaid, select, true {: "{said}"} other {}}. Write your answer to that, in keeping with what the two of you have already said in this thread, between {open} and {close}.)
main.noTime: The note did not settle on a time.
